assessment_summary:
0001: Merely labels the proposed solution; no mathematical claim requires justification.
0002: Validly announces the intended induction argument.
0003: Correctly defines the induction parameter n=|V(T)|.
0004: Correct: a one-vertex tree has no components after its sole vertex is removed.
0005: Correctly concludes that the n=1 condition is vacuous and begins the n=2 case.
0006: Correct: removing either vertex of a two-vertex tree leaves one vertex.
0007: Correct arithmetic: 1≤2/2=1.
0008: States a valid strong-induction hypothesis.
0009: Correctly fixes a tree with n≥3 for the inductive step.
0010: Correct: every finite tree with at least two vertices has a leaf.
0011: Correct: a leaf has a unique neighbor, and deleting it leaves a tree.
0012: Correct: T′ has n−1 vertices, so the induction hypothesis applies.
0013: Correctly begins the conclusion supplied by the induction hypothesis.
0014: Correctly completes the bound (n−1)/2.
0015: Correctly completes the assertion about components of T′−v.
0016: The cases v=w and v≠w are exhaustive.
0017: Correctly begins the analysis when v=w.
0018: Correct: deleting w isolates the leaf u as a singleton component.
0019: Correct: all remaining components are exactly those of T′−v.
0020: Correctly states that the singleton has size 1.
0021: Correct: 1≤n/2 for n≥2.
0022: Correctly invokes the induction-hypothesis bound for the other components.
0023: Correctly completes the bound (n−1)/2.
0024: Correct inequality: (n−1)/2≤n/2.
0025: Correctly concludes that v=w works in this case.
0026: Correctly introduces the complementary case v≠w.
0027: Correct in substance: u is attached to the component of T′−v containing w.
0028: Validly introduces an upper-bound calculation for the enlarged component.
0029: Correct: adjoining u increases the component containing w by exactly one.
0030: Correctly begins the resulting upper bound.
0031: Correctly completes the term (n−1)/2.
0032: Correct arithmetic: (n−1)/2+1=(n+1)/2.
0033: Correctly completes that displayed equality.
0034: Correctly begins comparing this upper bound with n/2.
0035: Correctly completes the expression (n+1)/2.
0036: Correct: (n+1)/2>n/2.
0037: Incorrect: an upper bound larger than n/2 does not show that the actual component exceeds n/2; it only shows that this induction estimate is insufficient.
0038: Reasonable as a decision to abandon the inconclusive induction route, though it does not repair step 0037.
0039: Validly introduces a separate algorithmic proof.
0040: Correctly starts from an arbitrary vertex and stops if it already satisfies the condition.
0041: Correct: failure of the condition means some component has more than n/2 vertices.
0042: Correctly instructs moving toward that component.
0043: Correct: exactly one neighbor of v0 lies in a given component of T−v0.
0044: Correctly defines iteration of the same rule.
0045: Correct in substance: every move enters the unique component having more than n/2 vertices.
0046: The termination conclusion is true, since after a move the component leading back has fewer than n/2 vertices, so the walk cannot backtrack or revisit a vertex in a finite tree; the stated wording omits this essential reason.
0047: Correctly characterizes the terminal vertex as one with no oversized component.
0048: Correctly completes the bound n/2.
0049: Validly begins an explanation of how component sizes change.
0050: Merely introduces the following component-size observations.
0051: Correct: the selected component in the direction of vi+1 has more than n/2 vertices.
0052: Correctly completes that inequality.
0053: Correct in substance for the new component containing vi: it consists of vi and all old components other than the selected one.
0054: Incorrect: if the previous large component has size s, the new component containing vi has size 1+(n−1−s)=n−s, not n−s−1.
0055: Consequently, the claimed bound below n/2−1 does not apply to the actual component; the correct conclusion is n−s<n/2.
0056: The strict decrease claim is nevertheless true: the back component has size n−s<s, while every forward component is a proper subset of the former s-vertex component.
0057: Correctly concludes that strict decrease over nonnegative integer sizes yields a vertex satisfying the condition.
0058: The theorem follows from the algorithmic argument, but saying it follows “by induction” is inaccurate because the attempted inductive step was abandoned.
0059: Merely a page number; it contains no proof claim.
